title: ICP-Brasil PAdES (AD-RB, AD-RT, AD-RC, AD-RA)
description: PAdES signatures under the ICP-Brasil signature policies (DOC-ICP-15.03: AD-RB, AD-RT, AD-RC and AD-RA; AD-RV has no PAdES form) with the icp-brasil trust profile and its signing and validation policies, through the library and the CLI. The Sandbox stands in for ICP-Brasil: its trust is added to the profile's (trustProfiles: Sandbox), so its certificates and its TSA play the part of an AC and an ACT; the first section shows that the profile alone trusts only the AC Raiz roots. AD-RA downloads its policy artifacts (LPA_PAdES and the PA) from ITI's repository, so that step needs the network. Tags name the policy (AD-RB…), the ICP-Brasil document (DOC-ICP-15.03) and a topic. It complements sandbox-basics and etsi-baseline: the checks they already show (revocation before signing, validity and key usage, the TSA's certificate, keys and digests, changed files, revocation after a time-stamp, certification) are not repeated here; only what the icp-brasil profile and its policies decide is.

inputs.title: A PDF signed with an ICP-Brasil certificate
inputs.description: Signed with a real ICP-Brasil certificate (an A1 or A3, a token, a cloud certificate, another signing product). The steps of the section 'Your files' validate it with the icp-brasil profile alone (the AC Raiz roots, no Sandbox) and raise its level; without the file they are skipped.

inputs.title: A PDF of yours to sign
inputs.description: Any PDF (a contract, a form, a PDF/A): it is signed under AD-RB and AD-RT with a Sandbox certificate, to see the policies on your own documents.

sections.title: The ICP-Brasil profile
sections.description: Its anchors are the AC Raiz roots bundled with SimpleSign.Brazil.IcpBrasil and its chain validation is ICP-Brasil's. A certificate that does not chain to them is refused before signing; the Sandbox's trust, added to the profile, lets the rest of the playbook sign with test certificates.

steps.title: Profile alone: a certificate outside ICP-Brasil is refused
steps.description: Only the AC Raiz roots are anchors: the Sandbox's chain is not trusted, and the library refuses to sign (UntrustedRoot).

steps.title: Profile with the Sandbox's trust added: signed
steps.description: The ICP-Brasil policies stay the profile's; only the Sandbox's anchors are added.

sections.title: Signature policies (DOC-ICP-15.03)
sections.description: Each policy writes its identifier and the hash of the policy document (signature-policy-identifier), the /Filter /PBAD_PAdES /SubFilter /PBAD.PAdES signature dictionary, and the level it needs. The newest version of the policy in force is chosen. Each signature is validated right after with the ICP-Brasil validation policy.

steps.title: AD-RB (basic reference)
steps.description: Signs under AD-RB: the signature-policy-identifier of the newest AD-RB in force and the PBAD.PAdES dictionary, no time-stamp (B-B). Validated right after with the ICP-Brasil validation policy; its file is reused by later steps.

steps.title: AD-RT (time reference): signature time-stamp from the ACT
steps.description: Signs under AD-RT: AD-RB plus a signature time-stamp from the ACT (here the Sandbox's TSA), giving B-T.

steps.title: AD-RC (complete references): validation data and a document time-stamp
steps.description: Signs under AD-RC: AD-RT plus the chain's certificates, CRLs and OCSP responses in the DSS and a document time-stamp over them (B-LTA).

steps.title: AD-RA (archival): AD-RC plus the PA, the LPA and its signature in the DSS
steps.description: The LPA_PAdES, its signature and the policy document are downloaded from ITI's repository, the LPA's signature is checked, and the three go into the DSS.

steps.title: AD-RC collecting CRLs before OCSP
steps.description: ICP-Brasil ACs publish CRLs; the revocation preference picks CRL first and OCSP as the fallback.

sections.title: How the library is called
sections.description: The same policies through the two-phase signer: the key signs elsewhere, as a token or a cloud certificate does (AD-RA embeds its artifacts and is made in one call only).

steps.title: AD-RT in two phases
steps.description: AD-RT through the two-phase signer: the library prepares the hash, the key signs it elsewhere (as a token or a cloud certificate would), and the library completes it. The result must equal a one-call AD-RT.

steps.title: AD-RC in two phases
steps.description: AD-RC through the two-phase signer: the validation data and the document time-stamp are added when the signature is completed.

sections.title: PDF documents
sections.description: What a PDF brings to an ICP-Brasil signature: a field to sign, a signature already there, a visible stamp in pt-BR (certification is in etsi-baseline).

steps.title: Sign the document's empty signature field
steps.description: Signs the empty signature field the document already has (Assinatura) instead of creating one, as forms prepared for signing expect.

steps.title: AD-RT with a visible stamp
steps.description: AD-RT with a visible stamp in pt-BR (signer, date in Brasília time, reason and location): the appearance must not affect the policy or the validation.

steps.title: A second signer (AD-RT) over the AD-RB document
steps.description: A second signer (RSA 3072, AD-RT) signs the AD-RB file in a new field: an incremental update that keeps the first signature intact. Its file is validated with both signatures.

sections.title: Validation with the ICP-Brasil profile
sections.description: The signatures above, validated with the ICP-Brasil validation policy (the default's constraints, and a signing certificate without digitalSignature or nonRepudiation fails); the files any validator must reject are in etsi-baseline and sandbox-basics.

steps.title: AD-RB
steps.description: Validates the AD-RB file with the ICP-Brasil profile and policy: valid, and its ETSI TS 119 102-2 report must be valid against the schema.

steps.title: AD-RT
steps.description: Validates the AD-RT file, its signature time-stamp included.

steps.title: AD-RC at the archival level
steps.description: Validates the AD-RC file at the archival-data level, which checks the document time-stamp and the validation data it protects.

steps.title: AD-RA at the archival level
steps.description: Validates the AD-RA file at the archival-data level, with the policy artifacts carried in its DSS.

steps.title: Two signers
steps.description: Validates the PDF signed by two signers: both signatures must be valid.

steps.title: Profile alone: the Sandbox's chain is not ICP-Brasil
steps.description: Validates the AD-RB file with the ICP-Brasil profile alone: the Sandbox's chain is not under the AC Raiz, so NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND. Shows the profile trusts only ICP-Brasil.

steps.title: Signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation (minimal signing policy, to validate)
steps.description: Signs with a certificate that has neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation, under the minimal signing policy and without validating, only to produce the file v-key-usage must reject.

steps.title: Signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation: not accepted
steps.description: Validates that file with the ICP-Brasil policy: the signing certificate's key usage does not allow signatures, so it is not accepted (INDETERMINATE).

sections.title: Where the ICP-Brasil policy differs
sections.description: The icp-brasil signing policy makes the checks of the generic policy that sandbox-basics runs (sandbox-strict: revocation of the whole chain, the chain to the anchors, the CA certificates' algorithms, the TSA's certificate), so those cases are shown there once; PlaybookPoliciesTests keeps the two in step. Where it decides otherwise, the step is here.

steps.title: CRL without nextUpdate: accepted
steps.description: The CRL served has no nextUpdate. The IOFE policy and the generic one refuse it (CRLNextUpdatePresent at FAIL: the CRL does not say until when it is current); the icp-brasil signing policy leaves that constraint at the default's IGNORE, so the CRL is used and, the certificate being good, the signature is made.

sections.title: Raising the level of an existing signature
sections.description: An AD-RT signature brought to B-LTA later (validation data and a document time-stamp), as AD-RC needs.

steps.title: AD-RT to B-LTA
steps.description: Raises the AD-RT signature to B-LTA afterwards (validation data and a document time-stamp), without signing again: what AD-RC needs, done later.

sections.title: Your files
sections.description: Files uploaded on the Playbook tab: a signature made with a real ICP-Brasil certificate (input:icp-signed) and a document to sign (input:document).

steps.title: Validate a real ICP-Brasil signature with the profile alone
steps.description: Only the AC Raiz roots and the ICP-Brasil chain validation are used: an intact signature by a valid, unrevoked ICP-Brasil certificate is accepted.

steps.title: Raise the real signature to B-LTA
steps.description: Raises the uploaded ICP-Brasil signature to B-LTA with the Sandbox's TSA, validating it with the ICP-Brasil profile alone: a real signature can be preserved the same way.

steps.title: Sign your document under AD-RB
steps.description: Signs the uploaded document under AD-RB with a Sandbox certificate, to see the policy applied to your own PDF (its structure, existing signatures, PDF/A).

steps.title: Sign your document under AD-RT
steps.description: Signs the uploaded document under AD-RT (with the Sandbox's time-stamp).
